Order No. 05/Dated: 16 May, 2024  Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 868 of 2021, in which cognizance under Sections 323, 341, 498A of the Indian Penal Code has been taken, the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per complaint, the allegation is that the marriage of complainant was solemnized with this petitioner on 24.07.2018 as per Hindu rites and customs.
After marriage, complainant went to her matrimonial home, where she lived quite well for some days.
Thereafter, accused persons started demanding Rs. 5,00,000/- cash as additional dowry.
Due to non-fulfillment of aforesaid demand of additional dowry, the accused persons started torturing her both physically and mentally and ultimately ousted her from matrimonial home.
Thereafter, the matter was pacified and the petitioner took the complainant to Kolkata, however, there also the petitioner started torturing her for the aforesaid demand of additional dowry.

It is further alleged that on 13.01.2020, the petitioner brutally assaulted the complainant and ousted from Kolkata house in two months pregnancy period,
but anyhow the complainant came to her matrimonial home, however her in-laws did not allow her to live there and they also ousted her from the matrimonial home.
Page 1|2
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that this case arises out of complaint for matrimonial dispute.
Petitioner is paying maintenance amount granted in favour of the complainant by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Koderma in Maintenance Case No. 75 of 2021.

1 abide by all terms and conditions, as imposed by this Court, in the case of granting anticipatory bail to this petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence, petitioner may be granted privilege of anticipatory bail.
On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P. appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against the petitioner, I am inclined to grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Koderma in connection with Complaint Case No. 868 of 2021 with the condition that he will co-operate in trial of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
